input.summary: Full ledger review completed against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure's first three paragraphs and adds nothing). I traced every limitation of all 16 claims (independent apparatus claim 1 and method claim 11 plus dependents 2-10 and 12-16), every one of the 27 entries in draft/numerals.md, every structure, relationship, definition, result and rationale sentence in draft/04 through draft/08 and draft/10, and every line-work and leader statement in figures/FIG-1.md through FIG-4.md. Each item traces to an exact affirmative disclosure passage: the branch-limited plurality of connectors ("whose allowable aggregate current is lower than the sum of the connector ratings"); the per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; the upstream branch current sensor ("measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"); the isolated local bus limited to "the connector interfaces and contactors"; the four stored per-session values; the allocation-interval arithmetic (measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve subtracted from the branch limit), sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot delivery and connector-sensor verification; the reduced pilot command, verification interval and one-at-a-time ordered shedding in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the limit; the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay; the leakage-threshold welded-contactor recording with inhibition of the other contactors on the same branch and the local fault indicator; the network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage behaviour, token expiry and tamper-evident meter sequence; and the service-input mapping with association stored only after the sensed channel agrees. I found no untraced technical assertion, no unsupported optional embodiment, no "by way of example" or "any outline" broadening language, no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative, and no numeral used for two different parts; all 27 numerals appear in exactly one figure brief with names identical to the numeral table and to the description, and no sectional views or section-line designations exist to reconcile. Two internal-consistency defects remain, both minor: FIG. 2 draws connector current sensor 124 with no depicted path to edge controller 106 even though the description states the coupling and claim 1 requires verification through that sensor, and the Background is missing a paragraph break so two paragraphs would merge on render. Both have filing-clean fixes below. Note for the record, as the brief requires: no prior-art search was run for this matter, so the art available in prior_art/ may be incomplete; that does not affect this source-fidelity review, which does not assess patentability, novelty or validity.

findings.title: Connector current sensor 124 is drawn with no depicted coupling to the edge controller in any figure, although the description and claim 1 both require that coupling
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (line-work paragraphs describing the isolated local bus branches) read against draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 2 paragraph, and draft/09-claims.md claim 1
findings.detail: The description states an affirmative electrical relationship that no drawing shows. In FIG. 2 the only path between the connector channel and the controller is the isolated local bus, and the brief routes that bus to exactly two destinations: "one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block and a second upward to the contactor outline." The description confirms the bus content is limited to "the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports," so the bus as drawn does not carry the connector current measurement. FIG. 1 draws each connector channel as a closed block, so the coupling cannot be inferred there either. The result is that connector current sensor 124 appears in the drawings as an element with no signal path to edge controller 106, while the specification and claim 1 both rely on that path. This is an omission relative to the text, not an unsupported assertion, so it is minor; the coupling itself is source-supported and only needs to be depicted.
findings.evidence: Description (FIG. 2 paragraph): "The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124." Claim 1: "verify the connector current resulting from the assigned current limit with the connector current sensor of that connector channel." Disclosure: "The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor." FIG-2.md line work: "Inside the rectangle it branches two ways: one branch to the left side of the control-pilot interface block and a second upward to the contactor outline." Description: "The isolated local bus 108 carries, between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, after the paragraph describing the isolated local bus, add: "A dashed line leaves the square outline representing the connector current sensor, runs left below the horizontal run and clear of the control-pilot interface block, and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle below the isolated local bus line, as the sensing connection by which the edge controller receives the measured connector current. It crosses no other line and no leader." This reuses the dashed sensing convention already used for the branch current sensor connection in FIG-1.md and FIG-3.md, adds no bus membership and no new numeral, and requires no change to FIG-1.md, to the numeral table, or to the description, which already recites the coupling.

findings.title: Missing paragraph break in the Background merges two distinct paragraphs on render
findings.where: draft/05-background.md, between the paragraph ending "...as the only remaining protection." and the paragraph beginning "Site controllers of this class also depend..."
findings.detail: Every other paragraph boundary in draft/05-background.md and in the other draft files is marked by a blank line, but these two paragraphs are separated by a single newline. On render the paragraph about vehicle response and uncommanded auxiliary load and the paragraph about network dependence will be joined into one block, producing a paragraph that changes subject mid-way and, in a numbered-paragraph filing, collapsing two paragraph numbers into one. No technical content is affected.
findings.evidence:
draft/05-background.md: "...with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection.
Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection to a remote management service for schedules, tariffs and driver authorization." Compare the preceding boundary in the same file, which has a blank line: "...rather than on the physical rating of any one connector.

A control function of this kind ordinarily issues a current limit..."
findings.fix: Insert a blank line in draft/05-background.md immediately after "...with the overcurrent device of the branch as the only remaining protection." so that "Site controllers of this class also depend on a network connection..." begins a separate paragraph. No wording changes.
